title: APPROVAL OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO FOREIGN-TRADE ZONE GENERAL PURPOSE OPERATING AGREEMENT NO. 26-10195 BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND BRINK’S GLOBAL SERVICES USA, INC., FTZ 202, SIT

RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO FOREIGN-TRADE ZONE GENERAL PURPOSE OPERATING AGREEMENT NO. 26-10195 BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND BRINK’S GLOBAL SERVICES USA, INC., FTZ 202, SITE NO. 73

Summary
: Staff requests approval of a First Amendment to Foreign-Trade Zone (FTZ) Operating Agreement No. 26-10195 between the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department) and Brink’s Global Services USA, Inc. (Brinks) to change the operational designation of the operator of FTZ 202, Site No. 73, located at 1821 South Soto Street, Los Angeles, California 90023. The Harbor Department, as the FTZ grantee, establishes Operating Agreements with FTZ site operators to oversee their FTZ operations. Brinks’ current FTZ Operating Agreement No. 26-10195 will expire on January 20, 2031. The First Amendment will change the operational designation from multi-usage to single-usage. This is a 0.18-acre site with a warehouse and office space located approximately 26 miles from the Port of Los Angeles (Port). The proposed First Amendment will not require funding by the Harbor Department. If the proposed amendment is approved, the Harbor Department will receive $10,000 annually from Brinks (per FTZ Tariff No. 2). The proposed action is aligned directly with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 3: Improved Financial Performance of Port Assets, Initiative 2: Increase the utilization of Port facilities and develop a plan to activate vacant port properties. FTZs are specifically designed to stimulate economic activity, utilize port property, and generate revenue. Approving developer and operator agreements directly activates port properties and designated zones, bringing in businesses that utilize the Port’s ecosystem. The proposed action also aligns with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 2: An Efficient, Secure, and Sustainable Supply Chain, Initiative 1: Facilitate supply chain efficiencies and terminal velocity with stakeholders, with continuous enhancements to the Port Optimizer product. FTZs provide distinct operational and regulatory advantages that streamline how cargo moves through the logistics chain. They allow cargo operators to defer, reduce, or eliminate customs duties. This financial and administrative incentive attracts cargo volumes, reduces customs clearance delays, and improves overall supply chain velocity for Port stakeholders.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) approve the proposed First Amendment to Foreign-Trade Zone Operating Agreement No. 26-10195 between the Harbor Department and Brinks; 3) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to the proposed First Amendment to Foreign-Trade Zone Operating Agreement No. 26-10195; and 4) adopt Resolution No. ____________.
